name: Nikolai Yudenich
summary: The most successful Russian field commander of the First World War - Erzurum in 1916 was a genuine victory in a war that gave Russia few - and the least successful of the White generals. His North-Western Army, raised in Estonia, made a dash for Petrograd in October 1919, reached the Pulkovo heights within sight of the city and was thrown back inside a fortnight. Estonia, negotiating its own peace with Moscow, then disarmed and interned what was left of him.
